name: Green River
label: Sub Pop
lede: Green River lasted three years, put out two EPs and one album, and split on Halloween 1987. The pieces became Mudhoney, Mother Love Bone and, eventually, Pearl Jam.

eras.title: The worst band in town, and a darker name
eras.text: Mark Arm and Steve Turner came up in Mr. Epp and the Calculations, a Bellevue punk band Arm has said enjoyed being called the worst in Seattle. In 1984 they pulled in Jeff Ament, Alex Vincent and Stone Gossard and named the new band after something much grimmer.

years.h: Mark Arm uses "grunge" to insult his own band
years.p: Writing to the Seattle fanzine Desperate Times under his real name, Mark McLaughlin, Arm calls Mr. Epp and the Calculations pure grunge. It's often cited as the word's first Seattle use.

years.h: Gossard turns up after the first rehearsal and stays
years.p: Arm and Turner recruit bassist Ament from Deranged Diction and drummer Alex Vincent. Stone Gossard, a high school friend of Turner and Vincent, joins after the first rehearsal at Turner's home on Mercer Island.
years.xp:
Ament met Arm and Turner through a Seattle coffee shop job. He didn't think much of Mr. Epp but was fed up with Deranged Diction.

The name came from a shirt Turner spotted. To Arm it recalled the Creedence song and also the Green River Killer, then all over the Washington news. Turner later called it "a dumb joke."

years.h: The first demos wait 32 years for a release
years.p: Green River cut them on June 23 at Seattle's Reciprocal Recording. They sit in the vault until a 2016 vinyl release.

years.cap: Newspaper ad for Green River, Sonic Youth and the U-Men at Gorilla Gardens, Seattle
years.h: Seattle gets its first look at Green River
years.p: The July 1984 debut mixes [[The Stooges|794c6bf2-3241-416f-9b8f-24e2d84a1c4b]] punk with '70s hard rock. Six months later the band shares a Gorilla Gardens bill with Sonic Youth and the U-Men.

eras.title: A guitarist quits before the record is out
eras.text: Steve Turner wanted garage rock and the others wanted Aerosmith, so he left before Come on Down came out. Bruce Fairweather took his place, a national tour went badly, and the band still made friends like Sonic Youth along the way.

years.big: "I should not be in this band. I'm fighting them so hard."
years.h: Turner leaves before the EP and the tour
years.p: Steve Turner, into 1960s garage rock, [[Billy Childish|23ef9155-df05-4e3a-8109-acb603f3146d]] and [[The Replacements|dc0d05ce-2f47-4962-b4fa-8631a0a51987]], says it of the heavier direction Green River was taking. Fairweather, Ament's old Deranged Diction bandmate, takes his place.
years.xp:
Turner told Rolling Stone: "I quit in the summer of '85 before the EP came out and before the tour, because I was dreading it." Gossard remembered the reason as Turner telling them: "You guys are playing way too complex for me."

Alex Vincent said the music got a little more rock once Turner left. Turner went back to school and, in 1988, into [[Mudhoney|e675295a-1efe-4247-aa3b-53b78d0cdffc]].

years.cap: Flyer for Sonic Youth, Upright Citizens and Green River at Le Club Hit, Seattle, August 16, 1985
years.h: Homestead puts out Come on Down, and almost nobody buys it
years.p: Green River's debut EP, on New York's Homestead Records, sells poorly. It's often called the first record by a grunge band anyway.
years.xp: Sonic Youth, who shared bills with Green River, later nodded to the title track in their song Nevermind (What Was It Anyway).

years.cap: Mark Arm at the Central Tavern, Seattle
years.h: At a Big Black show the PA dies and Arm throws the microphones
years.p: Touring behind Come on Down, Green River open for the [[Dead Kennedys|37c78aeb-d196-42b5-b991-6afb4fc9bc2e]] in San Francisco to an indifferent crowd. A later bill with [[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]] ends with the sound system gone.
years.xp:
Big Black withheld Green River's pay to cover a lost microphone that Rolling Stone's oral history prices at $250 to $300. [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] told Rolling Stone that everybody acts like an asshole when they're a kid.

Fairweather, on the Dead Kennedys night: "The audience wasn't really into them at all." A planned run with the U.K. Subs collapsed over visas, so the band played CBGB's and Hoboken with The U-Men instead.

years.h: Green River land two songs on Deep Six
years.p: C/Z Records' compilation has 10,000 Things and Your Own Best Friend, next to [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]], [[Soundgarden|153c9281-268f-4cf3-8938-f5a4593e5df4]], [[Skin Yard|0119843b-4d56-47b6-ac0d-11528259bf0a]], [[Malfunkshun|71f4a8ff-97ba-47c6-a729-7f87de77c796]] and The U-Men.

years.cap: Green River in a band portrait printed in The Rocket, Seattle, August 1, 1986
years.h: A single mixed on a Betamax deck
years.p: Stuck waiting for money to finish a Sub Pop EP, Green River release a 7-inch on Tasque Force. It's recorded by Gordon Raphael on an Akai deck that writes to Betamax cassettes.
years.xp: The B-side is Ain't Nothing to Do. Jack Endino mixed it, and told Rolling Stone it became the "green single" and that he did what he could on a "primitive little machine."

eras.title: Sub Pop's first record, then the split
eras.text: Green River gave Bruce Pavitt's Sub Pop its first non-compilation record, and Sub Pop gave the scene its word. By the end of the year the band had split down the middle: punk on one side, arena rock on the other.

years.cap: Mark Arm at the Central Tavern, Seattle, in a Mad Dog tee
q: Ultra-loose GRUNGE that destroyed the morals of a generation.
years.h: Sub Pop's first non-compilation release is a Green River EP
years.p: Recorded in summer 1986 with [[Jack Endino|d06cca33-9167-4049-b5ce-6a6aeff60a8d]] and held up for lack of money, Dry as a Bone comes out as Sub Pop SP-11.
years.xp:
Endino remembered the band as serious and meticulous in the studio. At the release show there was a green cake, and by the end of the night, he said, there was green frosting on everything.

Pavitt later admitted the catalog line was complete hyperbole. It stuck anyway.

years.h: Ament fills the Scream's guest list with label reps. Two come.
years.p: Opening for [[Jane's Addiction|e3434cc7-d348-491a-9dc8-325af3d9086d]] in Los Angeles, Green River find that Jeff Ament has put major-label reps on the list instead of friends. Mark Arm, voice shot after a San Francisco show, thinks the set is terrible.
years.xp:
Ament loved Jane's Addiction and came home wanting more of that kind of career. He told Rolling Stone: "At that Jane's Addiction show, something for me sort of broke."

Arm thought Ament and Gossard had turned careerist, and the gap between them didn't close.

years.big: "They said, 'This is the end.' I said, 'Okay, cool.'"
years.h: The band breaks up at a Halloween rehearsal
years.p: Arm's account of the moment Ament, Gossard and Fairweather told him and Alex Vincent they were leaving. The five agree to finish Rehab Doll first.
years.xp:
Arm wanted to go further into Australian punk like [[Feedtime|4775deb5-f3c3-45e2-b6c3-b66678aae511]] and [[The Scientists|b2cd8f3d-7049-4ebf-a5d6-52c08f6a59c0]]; Ament and Gossard wanted big Aerosmith-style rock. Arm told Rolling Stone it felt like a weight off his shoulders.

Vincent had the opposite reaction: "It was a terrible Halloween. I was literally devastated."

eras.title: One band becomes three
eras.text: The pieces scattered fast. Arm and Turner started Mudhoney. Ament, Gossard and Fairweather found singer Andrew Wood and formed Mother Love Bone, and after Wood's death Ament and Gossard headed toward Pearl Jam.

years.h: Mudhoney practices for the first time on New Year's Day
years.p: Arm and Turner, with [[Matt Lukin|299e8c0a-63ad-4d49-b492-d3740364da84]] and [[Dan Peters|3402566b-20dc-47f1-973b-2af1dedae702]], start Mudhoney two months after the split. They'd been jamming informally since early November.

years.h: Ament and Gossard get the glam band they wanted
years.p: With Fairweather and [[Malfunkshun|71f4a8ff-97ba-47c6-a729-7f87de77c796]] singer Andrew Wood, they form [[Mother Love Bone|a5585acd-9b65-49a7-a63b-3cc4ee18846e]].

years.cap: Community World Theater calendar flyer listing Green River, Tacoma
years.h: Green River's only album comes out after the band is over
years.p: Finished post-split and released on Sub Pop, Rehab Doll has Arm singing One More Stitch from under a grand piano and Fairweather on sitar.
years.xp:
[[Kim Gordon|19301485-ac9c-4dad-885b-cd8e8c8b4184]] of [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] sang on Swallow My Pride, but the band mixed most of her vocals out; Endino restored them on the later deluxe edition.

Ament later said they triggered a metal sound on the snare drum, and Vincent called the result grunge meets Poison.

years.h: Andrew Wood dies days before Mother Love Bone's debut
years.p: Wood dies of a heroin overdose on March 19. Ament and Gossard go on to [[Temple of the Dog|e9571c17-817f-4d34-ae3f-0c7a96f822c1]] with [[Chris Cornell|cbf9738d-8f81-4a92-bc64-ede09341652d]], then Pearl Jam.

years.h: One CD for the EP and the album
years.p: Sub Pop puts Dry as a Bone and Rehab Doll together on September 13, as the Seattle sound starts to sell.

eras.title: Three guitars, one more time
eras.text: Green River came back only for the occasional party. By then two of them were in Pearl Jam, two were in Mudhoney, and the old argument about punk versus rock didn't matter much.

years.h: Two songs in Las Vegas, with Pearl Jam as the host
years.p: At a Pearl Jam concert, Arm, Turner, Ament and Gossard play Swallow My Pride and Ain't Nothing to Do. [[Chuck Treece|ef661f53-d4b4-4903-811c-f3dcb1b970f3]] drums for Vincent, who is living in Japan.
years.xp: The Mudhoney fan history has Arm joining Pearl Jam for the encore, and calls it the first time the original members had played together since the split. A second reunion show followed in Reno on December 2.

years.h: Hype! gives a 1987 demo of Swallow My Pride a second life
years.p: Doug Pray's grunge documentary puts Green River's demo on its Sub Pop soundtrack.

years.h: All six play together for the first time since the '80s
years.p: The warm-up is July 10 at the Sunset Tavern in Ballard, three days before Sub Pop's anniversary show.

years.cap: Mark Arm at Sub Pop's 20th anniversary, Marymoor Park, Redmond, July 13, 2008
years.h: "A three-guitar army" at Sub Pop's birthday
years.p: Green River play Marymoor Park on July 13 with three guitars. Turner's verdict: it was a three-guitar army.
years.xp: Gossard told Rolling Stone it was "really fun," and that some of the songs are just really cool tunes.

years.h: The Melvins take Green River on their 25th anniversary tour
years.p: The reunited band plays a few more shows on the run, then stops again.

years.h: The 1984 demos finally come out on vinyl
years.p: The June 1984 Reciprocal Recording sessions, cut before Gossard joined, get their release.

years.h: Live at the Tropicana arrives on Jackpot Records
years.p: An archival live LP of Green River, out from the Portland label.

sources.title: Rolling Stone: Green River and Seattle's First 'Grunge' Album: The Oral History
